prerequisites: Matemáticas I, especially differential calculus and, very especially, integral calculus in one variable.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations.

Ability to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Ability to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Skill in the use of ICT
Capacity for critical and self-critical thinking
Ability to learn to work autonomously

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
The student must be able to model and solve situations involving the use of multivariable functions, fields, or differential equations.

syllabus_topics: Partial derivatives and rates of change.
Tangent plane, differentiability and linear approximation.
Change of variables: cylindrical and spherical coordinates.
Applications of double and triple integrals: areas, volumes, masses, centers of mass, Mean Value Theorem of integral calculus.
Vector fields. Conservative fields and potential. Curl and divergence.
Curve parametrization. Line and flux integrals of a vector field. Green's Theorem.
Parametric surfaces. Surface integrals. Divergence Theorem and Stokes' Theorem.
Elementary Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). Separable variable ODEs. Initial Value Problems (IVP).
Higher-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients, homogeneous and complete.
Laplace Transform and its application to solving IVPs of ODEs and systems of differential equations (SDEs).
assessment_rules: The final grade, out of a maximum of 10 points, is the weighted average of the scores obtained. To pass the course, the student must obtain at least five points (out of ten possible) in the overall calculation of the grade. In the ordinary call, assessment consists of 30% progress tests, 10% exercises or assignments, and 60% a final exam. In the extraordinary call, students have two options: either a 100% final exam or maintaining the continuous assessment score (40%) and taking a final exam for the remaining 60%. For a single final evaluation, the final exam covers 100% of the course content.
